notes: First labelled set taken after rx1_gain 25 -> 12 (2026-09-19). Every scan: 70 columns
x 1 cm, 6 rows x 2 cm, rover continuous at 100 mm/s, settle 0, num_buffers 1,
tx1/rx1 50/12, tx2/rx2 45/5, range_offset 0.378, no gaps, standoff 29-67 mm.
Empty scans bracket the session (18:08 and 18:29).
LABELS ARE IN A WALL FRAME, NOT THE SCAN'S. The operator's tape is fixed to the wall;
each raster starts wherever the rover was jogged to, and this set's starts span 9 cm
(rover_x at column 0: 2037.9 .. 2046.8 cm). So a label is converted to a column with
x_scan = label + tapeZeroRailCm[frame] - railX0Cm(scan)
where railX0Cm comes from the scan's own rover_x. tapeZeroRailCm is ONE number per
frame, fitted over the whole set against the confirmed detections only (weak detections
are dense enough that fitting against them matches any offset, which is how the first
attempt talked itself into a 10% scale error). Residual +-1.5 cm; the same labelled
position lands up to 3 cm apart in different scans, so THE TRUTH IS +-3 cm AND THE
POSITION METRIC IS LIMITED BY THE TAPE, NOT THE DETECTOR. Hence a 4 cm tolerance.
Frame A holds one labelled target, which fixes its own tape zero, so `1 pipe 12cm.json`
tests rating and false alarms but not position.
TWO ODOMETER FRAMES. The rover's position is relative to the last declared origin, and
between 18:12 and 18:16 it was re-declared: 'empty.json' and '1 pipe 12cm.json' read
~4.5 cm high against every later scan. Evidence: within each group the radar along-track
residual correlates 0.94-0.99 at the lag the rail predicts, across the groups 0.72-0.89
at a lag that does not fit. Detection is unaffected (each scan is self-contained); only
cross-scan work -- the empty reference, and this scoring -- needs the frame.

geometry.epsilonRNote: 4.84 (n = 2.2 exactly), the operator's own calculation, 2026-09-20. It is inside the band three independent measurements agree on, and the benchmark cannot separate 4.6 from 5.2 (all give 11/12 and 10/10), so the derived value is taken rather than the score-optimal one. The three: the front/back-face echo separation from permittivityEstimate is 33-36 cm -> er 4.8-5.8 at a 15.2 cm wall; the wall defect must image INSIDE the wall and the pipes behind it, which needs er >= ~4.8; and detection over both labelled sets falls away outside 4.6-5.2 (er 4 -> 10/12, 5.4 -> 9/12, 6 -> 9/12 and 9/10, 7 -> 9/12 and 7/10). Air is 1 on both sides: the layered model already uses air for the standoff gap and again beyond the back face. er and thickness are degenerate; what is measured is n*T = 33.4 cm.

knownFeatures.note: the wall's own defect/reflector -- operator-confirmed, present in every scan including the empties, and the ONLY such feature. Rated detections here are neither a hit nor a false alarm: a detector that did not see it would be broken. Images at 12-16 cm depth, i.e. at the back face, in every scan.
